podcast.body: The sound of this record, alongside "Lodger," significantly influenced the emerging New Romantics, shaping their musical direction. "The sound of his 1979 album, Lager, and especially his 1980 records, Scary Monsters and Super Creeps, were massive influences on the young New Romantics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album demonstrated a stark difference in reception between the UK and the US, being arguably Bowie's most British pop album. In the UK, it hit number one and was enthusiastically received as a major pop comeback, whereas in America, it was met with a shrug, peaking at a respectable but unremarkable number 12. Its full title was "Scary Monsters (and Supercreeps)." "But the David Bowie album, with perhaps the starkest difference in reception between the UK and the US, was 1980s scary monsters."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This album was intentionally commercial, partly due to Bowie's financial difficulties stemming from a detrimental management contract with Tony DeFrees. It served as a pivotal transition from the 70s to the 80s, centered around the song "Ashes to Ashes," and became highly influential on the emerging New Romantics scene and many future bands like Duran Duran and Depeche Mode. "Scary monsters and supercrepes was a great record, perhaps the perfect way to end the 70s and welcome the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, released in 1980, served as a benchmark for critical acclaim in Bowie's discography, with his 2002 album *Heathen* and 2013 album *The Next Day* both being described as his best work since this record. "Critics called it the best thing he'd done since Scary Monsters 22 years earlier."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This record marked a perfect end to the 1970s and a welcoming of the 1980s, finding a new balance between post-punk, art rock, and pop elements after Bowie's time in Berlin. Its centerpiece, "Ashes to Ashes," revisited the character of Major Tom and featured a groundbreaking, expensive music video that tapped into the emerging New Romantics scene in Britain. The album was hugely influential, particularly on artists like Morrissey and Johnny Marr of The Smiths. "Scary monsters and super creeps. The next record was great, the perfect way to end the 1970s and to welcome in the 1980s."

podcast.body: David Bowie made a groundbreaking video for a song from his "Scary Monsters" album in 1980, which he co-directed. This video utilized the Quantel Paintbox, a new computer graphics workstation, to achieve innovative special effects. "In 1980 he made a groundbreaking video for his song for Miss scary Monsters album which he co-directed."
